questions: Should the function modify the input DataFrame in-place or return a new DataFrame?
If the specified column does not exist in the DataFrame, should the function raise an error (as pandas drop does by default) or handle it silently (e.g., ignore)?
Is the index considered 'even' based on the integer position (0-based) after removing the column, or based on the original DataFrame's index values (which could be non-integer or non-sequential)?
Should the 'IsEvenIndex' column be added before or after removing the column, or does order matter (e.g., if the column to remove is named 'IsEvenIndex')?
What should happen if the DataFrame has a duplicate column name (e.g., multiple columns with same label)?
Should the function reset the index before determining evenness if the DataFrame has a non-default index (e.g., after filtering)?
Is the function required to handle non-DataFrame inputs (e.g., a dictionary) by converting them, or should it assume a DataFrame?
Should the 'IsEvenIndex' column be of boolean type (True/False) or integer (0/1) or something else?
